# MariaDB for Wikipedia RAG with MariaDB Vector. Start:  docker compose up -d --wait
# Ollama is not in here on purpose: run it on your machine so it can use the GPU.
# The tables are created by create_tables.py (setup.sh runs it), not mounted into the container:
# Docker on a Mac may not see files outside your home folder.
services:
  mariadb:
    image: mariadb:lts
    environment:
      MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD: wikirag
      MARIADB_DATABASE: wikirag
      MARIADB_USER: wikirag
      MARIADB_PASSWORD: wikirag
    ports:
      - "3307:3306"     # 3307 on your machine, so it does not collide with a local MariaDB on 3306
    volumes:
      - wikirag-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "healthcheck.sh", "--connect", "--innodb_initialized"]
      interval: 5s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  wikirag-data:

#!/bin/sh
# Set everything up in one go: Python packages, the embedding model, MariaDB in Docker, and the
# data with ready-made vectors. Takes a few minutes. Then:  .venv/bin/python app.py
#
#   ./setup.sh           # MariaDB in Docker (port 3307)
#   ./setup.sh --local   # use a MariaDB you already run; set DB_PORT etc. in .env first
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

need() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null || { echo "Missing: $1 — $2"; exit 1; }; }
need python3 "install Python 3.11 or later"
need ollama  "install from https://ollama.com/download"
[ "$1" = "--local" ] || need docker "install Docker Desktop, Colima or OrbStack, or run ./setup.sh --local"

echo "1/4  Python packages"
[ -d .venv ] || python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -q -r requirements.txt

echo "2/4  Embedding model bge-m3 (1.2 GB, once)"
ollama pull bge-m3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ollama pull failed. Is Ollama running? Start it from the menu bar or with: ollama serve"; exit 1; }

if [ "$1" != "--local" ]; then
  echo "3/4  MariaDB in Docker, and the tables"
  docker compose up -d --wait
else
  echo "3/4  The tables, in your own MariaDB"
fi
.venv/bin/python create_tables.py

echo "4/4  Articles, categories and vectors (downloads 110 MB the first time)"
.venv/bin/python load.py --vectors

echo
echo "Ready. Start the search page:  .venv/bin/python app.py   then open http://localhost:8000"

"""Search the articles from the command line.

    python search.py "who led Finland in the Winter War"
    python search.py --lang fi "talvisodan johtajat"
    python search.py --keyword "Mannerheim"        # ordinary full-text search, for comparison
    python search.py --category Talvisota "peace negotiations"   # only in this category

Works while embed.py is running: it searches whatever is embedded so far.
"""
import argparse, time
from common import connect, search

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("question")
parser.add_argument("--lang", help="only this language: fi, en or sv")
parser.add_argument("--category", help="only this Finnish category and its subcategories")
parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=10)
parser.add_argument("--keyword", action="store_true", help="full-text search instead of vectors")
parser.add_argument("--sql", action="store_true", help="print the SQL statement")
args = parser.parse_args()

con = connect()
cur = con.cursor()
t = time.time()
sql, rows = search(cur, args.question, mode="keyword" if args.keyword else "vector",
                   lang=args.lang, category=args.category, limit=args.limit)
if args.sql:
    print(sql, "\n")
print(f"({len(rows)} results in {(time.time() - t) * 1000:.0f} ms, including embedding the question)\n")
for r in rows:
    score = r.get("distance", r.get("score"))
    print(f"{score:7.4f}  {r['lang']}  {r['title']}\n          {r['url']}")
con.close()

# Wikipedia RAG with MariaDB Vector

> **Status:** steps 1–6 work, and step 8 is partly done: retrieval is measured against 37 test
> questions, the vector index is tuned, and search can be limited to a category. Still to do:
> hybrid search, chunks, and *Ask* (step 7). Anything marked **(to verify)** is not checked yet.
>
> **Developed against MariaDB 12.2.2** (Homebrew, macOS); the Docker route was tested with
> `mariadb:lts`, which was **12.3.3** in October 2026. Vector search needs 11.7 or later.

Ask a question in English, Finnish or Swedish and find the Wikipedia articles that answer it —
even when the answer is only written in another language. Then let an AI model write a short
answer that cites those articles.

Everything runs on a laptop: MariaDB stores the articles **and** their vectors in the same
database, and one SQL statement does the semantic search. No separate vector database — vectors are native in MariaDB.

![The search page: an English question finds the right treaty, with its Finnish and Swedish versions](docs/search-page.jpg)

Built as an example for doing RAG with MariaDB Vector. The data is *History of Finland* on
Wikipedia (a small dataset relative to the entire Finnish Wikipedia of over 500k articles):
29,460 articles — 19,285 Finnish, and the 5,254 English and 4,921 Swedish articles on the same
topics. 2,919 topics exist in all three languages.

Its companion, [mariadb-system-versioning-wikipedia](https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-system-versioning-wikipedia),
keeps every version of these articles in a system-versioned table: what did Wikipedia say on a
given day?

## Quick start

You need Python 3.11+, [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download) running, and Docker. Then:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-vector-wikipedia-rag.git
cd mariadb-vector-wikipedia-rag
./setup.sh                  # packages, the bge-m3 model, MariaDB in Docker, data and vectors
.venv/bin/python app.py     # the search page: http://localhost:8000
```

`setup.sh` took 2 min 50 s from a fresh clone (model and Docker image already downloaded;
otherwise add ~1.7 GB of downloads). The tutorial below builds the same thing step by step.

## What we found

- **Cross-language search works.** 37 test questions in Finnish, Swedish and English: the right
  article is in the top 5 for 76%, in the top 10 for 86%. Ordinary keyword search: 16% and 41%.
  Questions whose answer exists *only in Finnish* were found at rank 1 even when asked in English
  or Swedish.
- **The default vector index settings were not good enough.** With MariaDB's defaults (`M=6`,
  `mhnsw_ef_search=20`) the index found only 79% of the true 10 nearest articles, and for some
  questions none. With `M=16` and `ef_search=80`: 100%, in ~5 ms.
- **How you write the SQL decides whether the index is used.** The obvious query — vectors joined
  to articles, `ORDER BY distance LIMIT 10` — read 22,000 rows and took 50 ms. The same search in
  a subquery, joined afterwards, used the index: 1 ms.
- **Vector search and SQL filters combine in one statement.** A category and all its
  subcategories (a recursive query over the category tree) plus the vector ranking: exact results,
  10 ms for a small category — but 2 s for one that holds every article, because MariaDB then
  compares them all instead of using the index.
- **Questions about a fact in a person's life miss.** *"Who was the president of Finland from
  1956 to 1982?"* does not find *Urho Kekkonen* in the top 10: one vector for a whole
  biography sums up a life, not one fact in it. 3 of our 5 questions about presidents missed.
- **One vector per article finds the topic, not the fact.** *"Who led Finland in the Winter War"*
  finds the Winter War, not its leaders.

Details and how each was measured: step 8 and *Numbers*.

## Why inside MariaDB, and not a separate vector database

- **One statement does both.** Ranking by meaning and filtering by language, category or date is
  one SQL query with joins — not a vector search in one system, then a filter in another, then
  stitching the two together in code.
- **Nothing to keep in sync.** The vector sits in a row next to the article's id. Insert, update
  and delete are transactions; there is no second store that can fall behind or disagree.
- **The database tracks the work.** "Has a row in `article_vector`" = "is embedded", so the
  embedding job can stop and restart at any time (step 2). Search runs at the same time on
  whatever is committed, because MariaDB supports concurrent reads and writes on a vector index.
- **One thing to run, back up and secure.** No extra service, port or credentials.
- **What it costs:** you have to know your query shapes and index settings (step 8) — the
  optimizer does not yet always pick the vector index on its own.

## What you will have at the end

- A MariaDB database with 29,460 Wikipedia articles in three languages, each with a vector, and
  the category tree they belong to.
- A loader you can stop and restart: embed 100 articles, try search, embed 1,000 more.
- A small web page with two boxes:
  - **Search:** the closest articles, with language, distance and a link to Wikipedia. The SQL
    that produced the result is shown under it.
  - **Ask** *(later)*: an answer written by an AI model from the top articles, with numbered
    sources.
- A side-by-side comparison with ordinary keyword search (MariaDB `FULLTEXT`), so you can see
  what semantic search adds.

```
 FineWiki (Hugging Face)          Ollama (bge-m3, on your Mac)
        │                                   │
        ▼                                   ▼
  1. load.py  ──►  article  ──►  2. embed.py  ──►  article_vector
          │         (text)        (resumable)        (VECTOR + index)
          └──────►  article_category, category_link      │
                    (category tree)                       │
                     3. app.py  ◄── one SQL query ────────┘
                     search page  (+ "Ask" with an LLM, later)
```

## Choices, and why

### The data: FineWiki text for the History of Finland articles

- **Which articles:** everything in the Finnish category
  [Luokka:Suomen historia](https://fi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luokka:Suomen_historia), three levels of
  subcategories down, plus the English and Swedish articles on the same topics. The list and the
  category tree ship in this repo (`data/*.tsv`), so nobody has to walk the categories again.
- **Plus the main articles of named categories one level deeper.** Famous people and things have
  a category of their own, with their article inside it (*Luokka:Urho Kekkonen* holds *Urho
  Kekkonen*) — one level deeper than the walk, so the first version of the data had no
  *Mannerheim*, *Kekkonen*, *Ståhlberg*, *Paasikivi* or *Svinhufvud*. Walking that whole level
  would add ~1,260 categories and up to ~26,600 articles, mostly lists of politicians, city
  councillors and officers (and the band *Nightwish*): double the set, and diluted. Taking only
  the article with the same name as its category added 458 Finnish articles (and their Swedish
  and English versions), the presidents among them.
- **Which text:** [FineWiki](https://huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFW/finewiki) (August
  2025). Clean Markdown made from Wikipedia's rendered pages: templates filled in, no wiki markup
  noise. Raw wikitext would put `{{Infobox …}}` and reference syntax into the vectors.
- **Why not the live Wikipedia API:** fresher, but 28,000 requests run into Wikipedia's rate
  limit (200 requests a minute per IP address), and a bulk job like this belongs on the published
  dumps, not on Wikimedia's live servers.

### The model: bge-m3

We embed with [BAAI/bge-m3](https://huggingface.co/BAAI/bge-m3), run locally through
[Ollama](https://ollama.com/library/bge-m3).

Why this one, for this use case:

- **Three languages in one space.** It is multilingual (100+ languages), so an English question
  and a Finnish article land close together. Cross-language search is the point of this demo.
- **Tested on Wikipedia, including Finnish.** Its paper reports results on
  [MIRACL](https://github.com/project-miracl/miracl), a retrieval benchmark built from Wikipedia
  in 18 languages, Finnish among them — the closest public test to what we do.
  Paper: [BGE M3-Embedding (arXiv 2402.03216)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03216).
- **Tested on MariaDB for cross-language search.** A mariadb.org post compared three models on
  MariaDB Vector, searching English titles with Dutch queries: the English-only all-MiniLM found
  the right one first 14% of the time, bge-m3 59%, EmbeddingGemma 60% (with its task prompts).
  Different languages, same lesson: an English-only model fails at this, and you should test
  before you commit. [MariaDB Vector in Laravel: insights on choosing an embedding model](https://mariadb.org/mariadb-vector-in-laravel-insights-on-choosing-an-embedding-model/)
- **Long input: up to 8,192 tokens.** Most articles fit whole, which is what lets us embed whole
  articles (next section).
- **Open and local.** MIT licence, ~570 M parameters, runs on an M4 laptop. No API key, no cost,
  no text leaves the machine — and anyone following this tutorial can run the same model.
- **Easy to install.** `ollama pull bge-m3` — no PyTorch or Python ML stack needed. Any language
  that can make an HTTP call can embed a question.

Models we did **not** choose:

| Model | Why not |
|---|---|
| [nomic-embed-text](https://ollama.com/library/nomic-embed-text) (v1) | Long input (8,192 tokens) and already on many laptops, but trained for **English**. Finnish and Swedish questions would match poorly. |
| [multilingual-e5-large](https://huggingface.co/intfloat/multilingual-e5-large) | Good multilingual model, but reads only **512 tokens** — about one paragraph — so whole articles would be cut off after the first paragraph. Fine if we chunk. |
| [EmbeddingGemma-300m](https://huggingface.co/google/embeddinggemma-300m) | As good as bge-m3 in the test above, smaller and faster. But it reads only **2,048 tokens**, so long articles would be cut off. A strong choice if we chunk — worth testing in step 8. |
| [all-MiniLM-L6-v2](https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2) | The common tutorial default. Fast and small, but English-only and reads at most 256 tokens. |
| OpenAI `text-embedding-3` / Cohere Embed v3 | Good quality, but need an API key and cost money per call, and the text leaves the laptop. Not something a free, local tutorial should depend on. |

Newer models score higher on the [MTEB leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard)
(for example [Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B)). bge-m3 is
the safer default: widely used, well documented, tested on Finnish Wikipedia. Swapping the model
is one setting; comparing two models is a good project in itself.

### What we vectorize: the whole article (for now)

**This demo stores one vector per article**, made from the whole article text (title + text).

Why start there:

- **Simple:** one article = one row = one vector. Easy to explain, easy to link back to Wikipedia.
- **Small:** 29,460 vectors (~120 MB). Fast to search.
- **Good at "which article is about this?"** — which is what the Search box shows.

What it costs — **the open question**:

- **Long articles get cut.** bge-m3 reads 8,192 tokens; the rest is ignored. Measured: 290 of
  29,460 articles (1.0%) are longer, e.g. *Talvisota*. Few, but they are often the most important
  ones.
- **Details get diluted.** One vector sums up the whole article. A fact in paragraph 30 barely
  moves it, so very specific questions match worse. Seen in practice: *"who led Finland in the
  Winter War"* finds the Winter War articles, not the leaders.
- **Answers need a big context** (for *Ask*, later). Sending the top five whole articles to an
  AI model can be 30,000–50,000 tokens: fine for a cloud model, too much for most small local
  models.

The alternative is **chunks**: cut each article into ~200–400-word pieces, one vector each
(~150,000 vectors). Better for precise matches, smaller AI context, but more rows, more
embedding time and one more idea to explain. Our plan: build whole-article first, measure, and
try chunking in step 8 (*Optimize*) together with the other settings. The table design already
allows it (see step 2).

### Search first; "Ask" later; no chat

- The **search** is what MariaDB does, so it is the centre: it shows the results *and* the SQL.
  The first version is search only.
- **Ask** (step 7, later) gives one answer to one question, with sources. That is the "G" in RAG
  and what people expect to see.
- **No multi-turn chat.** Keeping a conversation adds code and nothing about MariaDB. You can
  add it.

### Where things run (Mac M4)

- **MariaDB** in Docker (`mariadb:lts`), or a local Homebrew install. Vector search needs
  MariaDB 11.7 or later.
- **Ollama on the Mac itself, not in Docker.** Docker on a Mac cannot use the Apple GPU, so
  embedding inside a container would be several times slower.
- **Python** for the scripts, in a virtual environment.

## Tutorial

### Step 0 — What you need

| Requirement | Version / amount | Why | Check with |
|---|---|---|---|
| Laptop | Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or later), or Linux | Embedding runs locally; Apple GPU makes it fast | — |
| Memory | 16 GB recommended, 8 GB minimum *(to verify)* | bge-m3 uses ~2 GB while embedding, MariaDB ~1 GB | — |
| Free disk | ~3 GB | bge-m3 1.2 GB, database ~0.6 GB, MariaDB image 0.4 GB | `df -h ~` |
| Internet | ~2 GB to download, once | The model, the MariaDB image, the ready-made vectors | — |
| MariaDB | **11.7 or later** (vector search) — `mariadb:lts` in Docker, or a local install | Stores articles and vectors | `mariadb --version` |
| Docker | Docker Desktop, Colima or OrbStack — only if you run MariaDB in Docker | Runs MariaDB | `docker ps` |
| Ollama | latest | Runs the embedding model on the Mac's GPU. Install it on the Mac, **not** in Docker | `ollama --version` |
| Python | 3.11 or later | The load, embed and search scripts | `python3 --version` |
| Accounts / API keys | **None** | Everything in steps 1–6 and 8 is free and local | — |

Time: steps 0–3 take a few minutes. Then either load the ready-made vectors (~3 minutes) or
embed everything yourself (~5 hours on a MacBook Air M4). `./setup.sh` does steps 0–4 with the
ready-made vectors; the steps below are what it does.

```bash
ollama pull bge-m3
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Step 1 — Start MariaDB

```bash
docker compose up -d --wait
```

`docker-compose.yml` starts `mariadb:lts` with a database, user and password all called
`wikirag`, on **port 3307** — not the usual 3306, so it does not collide with a MariaDB you may
already run. `--wait` returns when MariaDB is ready to take connections.

**Using your own MariaDB instead** (11.7 or later):

```sql
CREATE DATABASE wikirag;
CREATE USER wikirag@localhost IDENTIFIED BY 'wikirag';
GRANT ALL ON wikirag.* TO wikirag@localhost;
```

and put its port in a file called `.env` in this folder:

```
DB_PORT=3306
```

The scripts read `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DB_NAME` from `.env` or
the environment (`common.py`). The defaults are for a local demo only. `./setup.sh --local`
sets everything up against your own MariaDB.

### Step 2 — Create the tables

```bash
python create_tables.py
```

It runs [schema.sql](schema.sql) over the normal connection — the same way for Docker and a local
MariaDB. (Mounting `schema.sql` into the container would be the usual Docker way, but Docker on a
Mac only sees files in your home folder, so a clone elsewhere fails.)

The tables in [schema.sql](schema.sql):

```sql
CREATE TABLE article (
  lang          CHAR(2)      NOT NULL,      -- fi, en, sv
  page_id       INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,      -- Wikipedia's own id, per language
  rev_id        INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,      -- the version we have
  wikidata_id   VARCHAR(20),                -- same topic across languages, e.g. Q33 = Finland
  title         VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  url           VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
  date_modified DATETIME,                   -- when this version was saved
  text          MEDIUMTEXT   NOT NULL,      -- clean Markdown from FineWiki
  PRIMARY KEY (lang, page_id),
  KEY (wikidata_id),
  FULLTEXT (title, text)                    -- for keyword search
);

CREATE TABLE article_vector (
  lang       CHAR(2)      NOT NULL,
  page_id    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  model      VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,         -- which model made this vector
  truncated  BOOL         NOT NULL,         -- article was longer than the model reads
  embedding  VECTOR(1024) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (lang, page_id),
  VECTOR INDEX (embedding) M=16 DISTANCE=cosine
);

CREATE TABLE category_link (                -- the category tree
  parent  VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  child   VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (parent, child),
  KEY (child)
);

CREATE TABLE article_category (             -- which categories an article is in
  lang      CHAR(2)      NOT NULL,
  page_id   INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  category  VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (lang, page_id, category),
  KEY (category)
);
```

Why it looks like this:

- **Vectors in their own table.** A column with a `VECTOR INDEX` must be `NOT NULL`, so a vector
  can only exist once it is computed. *"Has a row in `article_vector`"* = *"is embedded"*. That
  one fact makes the embedding job resumable. Chunks, later, would be one more table of the same
  shape.
- **`(lang, page_id)` as the key.** Page ids are only unique within one language's Wikipedia.
  Keeping Wikipedia's own ids means every result links back to the live page.
- **`wikidata_id` ties the languages together.** *Talvisota*, *Winter War* and *Vinterkriget* share
  `Q134949`. That is how results show their other-language versions, and how evaluation counts a
  hit in any language.
- **`DISTANCE=cosine`** because bge-m3 is trained for cosine similarity. **`M=16`** instead of the
  default 6: measured in step 8.
- **Categories in Finnish only.** They come from Finnish Wikipedia. Swedish and English articles
  get the categories of the Finnish article on the same topic, so a category filter works in all
  three languages.
- **The category tree as parent–child pairs.** Categories nest (*Suomen historia* → *Talvisota* → …)
  and a category can have several parents. A recursive query walks it (step 5).

### Step 3 — Load the articles

```bash
python load.py
```

- Loads the articles from `data/articles-fi.parquet`, `-sv` and `-en` (29,460 articles, cut out
  of FineWiki, 57 MB in total) and the categories from `data/*.tsv`. All in this repo. Takes a few
  seconds.
- Safe to run again: rows already loaded are skipped.

**How we cut the articles out of FineWiki** (`prepare.py` — you don't need to run it):

1. **The article list.** `find_articles.py` walks the category
   [Luokka:Suomen historia](https://fi.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luokka:Suomen_historia) three levels
   down with the Wikipedia API: 1,017 categories, 1,760 links between them, **19,754 articles**
   (19,296 from the walk, 458 main articles of named categories one level deeper), 10 minutes. The results are in the repo: `data/articles-fi.tsv`, `data/category-links-fi.tsv`,
   `data/article-categories-fi.tsv`.
2. **Only three languages.** FineWiki is 185 GiB in total, but stored as one folder per language:
   `fiwiki` 1.65 GB (2 files), `svwiki` 3.1 GB (3 files), `enwiki` 37.7 GB (15 files).
3. **Only the columns we need.** The files are Parquet: stored column by column. DuckDB reads them
   straight from Hugging Face and fetches only the columns we ask for — the raw `wikitext`
   column, about two thirds of each file, is never downloaded. Nothing large is stored on disk.
4. **Finnish by `page_id`, Swedish and English by `wikidata_id`** — the same topic has the same
   Wikidata id in every language.
5. **Keep the newest version.** FineWiki sometimes has several versions of one article
   (4 of *Talvisota*), so we keep the one with the highest `rev_id`.

What came out:

| | Articles | Text | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| fi | 19,285 of the 19,754 in the list | 73 MB | 4 min (2 files) |
| sv | 4,921 | 14 MB | ~30 min (3 files, with waits) |
| en | 5,254 | 28 MB | 82 min (15 files, ~5.5 min each) |

The 469 missing Finnish articles are newer than FineWiki's August 2025 snapshot, or pages
FineWiki leaves out. Times are on a ~3 MB/s home connection.

**Hugging Face limits requests.** Reading single columns means ~3,000 small requests per file,
and anonymous users may only make so many per 5 minutes. `prepare.py` then waits 5 minutes and
continues. Logging in with a free Hugging Face token raises the limit *(to verify)*.

### Step 4 — Embed, a bit at a time — or load ready-made vectors

**The quick way:** load the vectors we computed (same model, same settings) and go to step 5.

```bash
python load.py --vectors      # downloads data/vectors-bge-m3-*.parquet (119 MB) the first time
```

From an empty database to searchable: 2 min 40 s for the first version of the data (most of it is MariaDB building the vector index
as the rows arrive). Checked: `evaluate.py` gives the same numbers on a fresh copy.

**Or compute them yourself** — the point of the tutorial, and what you need for another model:

```bash
python embed.py --limit 100     # first 100 articles, then stop
python embed.py                 # everything that is left
```

- Picks articles that have no vector yet, sends them to Ollama in batches, writes the vectors,
  commits after each batch.
- Stop it with Ctrl-C at any time. Run it again and it continues where it stopped.
- **Order:** articles that exist in all three languages first. Those are usually the important
  topics, so the first 100 already give useful results, in every language.
- Prints progress: articles done, articles per minute, time left.
- Articles longer than the model reads (8,192 tokens) are cut, and marked `truncated = 1`.

**A trap in Ollama.** Setting the context to 8,192 tokens (`num_ctx`) is not enough. An embedding
has to fit in one *batch*, and Ollama's default batch is 2,048 tokens — longer texts are refused,
or silently cut to the first ~1,500 words. Set both (see `common.py`):

```python
"options": {"num_ctx": 8192, "num_batch": 8192}
```

### Step 5 — Search from SQL

Embed the question with the same model, then:

```sql
SET mhnsw_ef_search = 80;     -- see step 8

SELECT a.lang, a.title, a.url, v.distance
FROM (SELECT lang, page_id, VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(embedding, VEC_FromText(?)) AS distance
      FROM article_vector
      ORDER BY distance
      LIMIT 10) AS v
JOIN article a USING (lang, page_id)
ORDER BY v.distance;
```

**Why the subquery.** MariaDB uses the vector index when `ORDER BY VEC_DISTANCE_…(column, vector)
LIMIT n` stands directly on the table that has the index. Written as one flat join —
`FROM article_vector v JOIN article a … ORDER BY distance LIMIT 10` — `EXPLAIN` still names the
index, but the query read 22,000 rows and took 50 ms instead of 1 ms (step 8). A language filter
can go inside the subquery (`WHERE lang = 'sv'`): still the index, still exact, 8 ms.

**With a category** — vectors, a recursive walk of the category tree, and joins, in one statement:

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE cats AS (
  SELECT CAST('Suomen sisällissota' AS VARCHAR(255)) AS name
  UNION
  SELECT l.child FROM category_link l JOIN cats ON l.parent = cats.name)
SELECT a.lang, a.title, VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(v.embedding, VEC_FromText(?)) AS distance
FROM article_vector v
JOIN article a USING (lang, page_id)
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM article_category c JOIN cats ON c.category = cats.name
              WHERE c.lang = a.lang AND c.page_id = a.page_id)
ORDER BY distance
LIMIT 10;
```

- `CAST(… AS VARCHAR(255))`: in a recursive query the first row fixes the column size. Without it,
  a short start category fails with *"Data too long for column 'name'"* as soon as a subcategory
  has a longer name.
- MariaDB runs this category-first: it finds the category's articles, then compares only those.
  Exact, and fast for small categories (step 8 has the numbers).

### Step 8 — Optimize the solution

The first version uses simple defaults on purpose. This step is about measuring and tuning them.

**How to measure.** [data/test-questions.tsv](data/test-questions.tsv) has 37 questions about
the history of Finland — 13 in English, 11 in Swedish, 13 in Finnish — each with the article that
answers it. For 4 of them that article exists only in Finnish; 5 ask about presidents. A hit is the answer in *any*

```bash

python index_recall.py                 # vector index against exact search, for several ef_search
```

#### Measured: retrieval quality

`python evaluate.py --runs 5`, MariaDB 12.2.2, `M=16`, `ef_search=80`, MacBook Air M4:

| | Questions | hit@1 | hit@5 | hit@10 | MRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Vector** | all 37 | 57% | 76% | 86% | 0.65 |
| | in English | 54% | 69% | 77% | 0.61 |
| | in Swedish | 82% | 82% | 100% | 0.84 |
| | in Finnish | 38% | 77% | 85% | 0.52 |
| | answer only in Finnish | 100% | 100% | 100% | 1.00 |
| | the first 32 (no presidents) | 62% | 81% | 94% | 0.71 |
| **Keyword** (`FULLTEXT`) | all 37 | 11% | 16% | 41% | 0.15 |
| | answer only in Finnish | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0.00 |

Latency: embedding the question 28 ms (median); the SQL query 16 ms (vector, including the join
and Python) and 26 ms (keyword). Single machine, 5 runs per question. Full output:
[data/evaluation.txt](data/evaluation.txt).

What it says:

- **Vector search is far better than keyword search here.** Keyword search cannot cross
  languages at all, and MariaDB's `FULLTEXT` has no Finnish stemming: *Mannerheim* matches 649
  articles, *Mannerheimin* 305, *Mannerheimille* 43 — each word form is a different search.
- **Adding 1,115 articles did not hurt.** The first 32 questions score as before (81% / 94%) on
  the larger set; the lower total comes from the 5 new questions about presidents, 3 of which miss
  completely (Kekkonen, Svinhufvud, and Mannerheim asked in Finnish). A fact in a long
  biography is the case one vector per article handles worst.
- **The other misses are near-misses.** 6 of the first 32 not in the top 5; 4 of those are at rank 6–9. The
  vector finds the neighbourhood: asked for the emperor's 1899 decree that limited Finnish
  autonomy (*Helmikuun manifesti*), it ranks first his 1891 rescript on the same autonomy
  (*Rauhoitusreskripti*).
- **Finnish questions have the lowest hit@1** (38%). Many Finnish articles are long; one vector
  for a long article is less focused. Chunks are the obvious next test.
- 37 questions is a small set: one question is about 3 percentage points. Good for comparing settings,
  not for claiming a precise number.

| no index (exact) | — | 100% | 100% | 1,800–2,100 ms |

#### What else to tweak

| What | Options to try | What it changes |
|---|---|---|
| **Chunking** | Whole article (default) · fixed pieces of 200–400 words with overlap · one piece per section (split on the Markdown headings) | Precise questions match better with chunks; more rows and longer embedding time. Chunks go in a separate `chunk_vector` table |
| **What text goes in** | Whole text (default) · title + first section only · drop tables, lists and "See also" | Less noise in the vector; long articles stop getting cut off |
| **Embedding model** | bge-m3 (default) · a newer one, e.g. Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B · EmbeddingGemma or multilingual-e5 together with chunks | Quality per language, speed, vector size. A new model means embedding everything again — put it in a second table to compare side by side |
| **Vector index settings** — *done, see above* | `M` in `VECTOR INDEX … M=…` · `SET mhnsw_ef_search = …` | Accuracy against speed and memory |
| **Hybrid search: full-text + vector** | Combine the `MATCH … AGAINST` result and the vector result into one ranking with **Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)**, in one SQL statement (see below) | Names and exact terms (people, places, years) are often found better by keywords; meaning by vectors |
| **Language preference** | Measure it, then try: one result per topic (next row), or a fixed number of results per language | Seen in practice: English questions get mostly English and Swedish articles, Finnish questions Finnish and Swedish. Cross-language works, but the question's own language wins |
| **One result per topic** | Group by `wikidata_id` so fi, en and sv versions of the same article count as one result | Fewer near-duplicate results |
| **Filters** — *language and category done* | Article length, edit date (`date_modified`), links | More SQL next to the vector search |
| **Embedding speed** | Batch size · Ollama's `num_ctx` and `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL` · sentence-transformers on the Apple GPU instead of Ollama | Time to embed everything — ~5 hours now; matters for anyone embedding their own data or a bigger set |

**Hybrid search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.** Full-text and vector search give scores that
cannot be compared — a `MATCH` relevance and a cosine distance are different units. RRF ignores
the scores and uses only each article's *position* in each list: score = 1 / (60 + rank in the
full-text list) + 1 / (60 + rank in the vector list). An article that ranks well in either list
comes out near the top; one that ranks well in both comes out first. A plain `JOIN` of the two
lists would keep only articles found by both and lose good results found by just one.

- MariaDB docs: [Optimizing Hybrid Search Query with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/sql-structure/vectors/optimizing-hybrid-search-query-with-reciprocal-rank-fusion-rrf)
- Background: [Can you do RAG with Full Text Search in MariaDB?](https://mariadb.org/rag-with-full-text-index-search/) (mariadb.org)

In the demo: a third mode on the search page, **Hybrid**, next to *Vector* and *Keyword*, so the
same question can be compared in all three. Measured with the test set like everything else.
Measured so far: `FULLTEXT` has no Finnish stemming, so each word form is its own search (see
*Measured: retrieval quality*) — a reason to expect hybrid search to help mostly with names and
exact terms. *(Hybrid: to do.)*

"""Compute a vector for every article that does not have one yet.

    python embed.py --limit 100     # 100 articles, then stop
    python embed.py                 # everything that is left

Stop with Ctrl-C at any time and run again to continue: every batch is committed, and the
next run picks up the articles that still have no row in article_vector.

Order: topics that exist in all three languages first, the language versions of one topic
together. So the first 100 articles already give results in fi, en and sv.
"""
import argparse, time
from common import connect, embed, vector_text, MODEL

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, help="stop after this many articles")
parser.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=8, help="articles per call to Ollama")
args = parser.parse_args()

NEXT = """
SELECT a.lang, a.page_id, a.title, a.text
FROM article a
LEFT JOIN article_vector v USING (lang, page_id)
LEFT JOIN (SELECT wikidata_id, COUNT(*) AS langs FROM article GROUP BY wikidata_id) t
       USING (wikidata_id)
WHERE v.page_id IS NULL
ORDER BY t.langs DESC, a.wikidata_id, a.lang
LIMIT ?"""

SAVE = """INSERT INTO article_vector (lang, page_id, model, truncated, embedding)
          VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, VEC_FromText(?))"""

con = connect()
cur = con.cursor()
cur.execute("SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM article), (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM article_vector)")
total, already = cur.fetchone()
goal = min(total - already, args.limit or total)
print(f"{already} of {total} articles already embedded. Embedding {goal} now with {MODEL}.")

done = tokens = 0
start = time.time()
try:
    while done < goal:
        cur.execute(NEXT, (min(args.batch, goal - done),))
        batch = cur.fetchall()
        if not batch:
            break
        texts = [f"{title}\n\n{text}" for _, _, title, text in batch]
        try:
            vectors, n = embed(texts, truncate=False)
            truncated = [False] * len(batch)
        except ValueError:
            # At least one article is longer than the model reads: do them one by one,
            # cutting only the long ones, and remember which were cut.
            vectors, truncated, n = [], [], 0
            for text in texts:
                try:
                    v, k = embed([text], truncate=False)
                    truncated.append(False)
                except ValueError:
                    v, k = embed([text], truncate=True)
                    truncated.append(True)
                vectors += v
                n += k
        cur.executemany(SAVE, [(lang, page_id, MODEL, cut, vector_text(vec))
                               for (lang, page_id, _, _), vec, cut in zip(batch, vectors, truncated)])
        con.commit()
        done += len(batch)
        tokens += n
        mins = (time.time() - start) / 60
        rate = done / mins
        print(f"{already + done}/{total}  {rate:.0f} articles/min  {tokens / mins / 60:.0f} tokens/s"
              f"  ~{(goal - done) / rate:.0f} min left   last: {batch[-1][0]} {batch[-1][2]}")
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    con.rollback()
    print("\nStopped. Run again to continue.")

cur.execute("SELECT COUNT(*), SUM(truncated) FROM article_vector")
n, cut = cur.fetchone()
print(f"Embedded: {n} of {total}. Cut because too long: {cut or 0}.")
con.close()

"""Measure how well search finds the right article, and how fast.

    python evaluate.py                    # vector and keyword search, 3 runs each
    python evaluate.py --runs 5 --misses  # more runs, and list the questions that failed

Reads data/test-questions.tsv: a question in fi, sv or en, and the Finnish title of the article
that answers it. A hit is that article in ANY language — the Finnish, Swedish or English version
of the same topic (same wikidata_id) all count.

Reports, per search mode:
  hit@1, hit@5, hit@10   share of questions where the answer is in the top 1, 5, 10 results
  MRR                    mean reciprocal rank: 1 for first place, 1/2 for second, ... 0 if not in top 10
  latency                median and slowest of all runs, split into embedding the question and the SQL
"""
import argparse, csv, statistics, time
from common import connect, embed, search

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=3, help="repeat each search this many times for timing")
parser.add_argument("--modes", default="vector,keyword")
parser.add_argument("--misses", action="store_true", help="list questions whose answer was not in the top 5")
parser.add_argument("--questions", default="data/test-questions.tsv", help="the test questions")
args = parser.parse_args()

con = connect()
cur = con.cursor()
with open(args.questions) as f:
    questions = list(csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t"))

# The answer as a topic: its wikidata_id, or its page_id if it has none.
for q in questions:
    cur.execute("SELECT wikidata_id, page_id FROM article WHERE lang = 'fi' AND title = ?",
                (q["expected_fi_title"],))
    q["wikidata_id"], q["page_id"] = cur.fetchone()


def rank_of_answer(q, rows):
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        if (q["wikidata_id"] and r["wikidata_id"] == q["wikidata_id"]) or \
           (r["lang"] == "fi" and r["page_id"] == q["page_id"]):
            return i
    return None


def summary(group):
    ranks = [q["rank"] for q in group]
    hit = lambda k: sum(1 for r in ranks if r and r <= k) / len(ranks)
    mrr = sum(1 / r for r in ranks if r) / len(ranks)
    return f"{len(group):>3} | {hit(1):5.0%} | {hit(5):5.0%} | {hit(10):5.0%} | {mrr:.2f}"


for mode in args.modes.split(","):
    embed_ms, sql_ms = [], []
    for q in questions:
        for run in range(args.runs):
            vector = None
            if mode == "vector":
                t = time.perf_counter()
                [vector], _ = embed([q["question"]])
                embed_ms.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000)
            t = time.perf_counter()
            _, rows = search(cur, q["question"], mode, limit=10, vector=vector)
            sql_ms.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000)
        q["rank"] = rank_of_answer(q, rows)
        q["top"] = rows[0]["title"] if rows else "-"

    print(f"\n## {mode} search — {len(questions)} questions, {args.runs} runs each\n")

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS article (
  lang          CHAR(2)      NOT NULL,      -- fi, en, sv
  page_id       INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,      -- Wikipedia's own id, per language
  rev_id        INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,      -- the version we have
  wikidata_id   VARCHAR(20),                -- same topic across languages, e.g. Q33 = Finland
  title         VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  url           VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
  date_modified DATETIME,                   -- when this version was saved
  text          MEDIUMTEXT   NOT NULL,      -- clean Markdown from FineWiki
  PRIMARY KEY (lang, page_id),
  KEY (wikidata_id),
  FULLTEXT (title, text)                    -- for keyword search
) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;

-- A vector exists only once it is computed: a VECTOR INDEX column must be NOT NULL.
-- "Has a row here" = "is embedded". That is what makes embed.py resumable.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS article_vector (
  lang       CHAR(2)      NOT NULL,
  page_id    INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  model      VARCHAR(50)  NOT NULL,         -- which model made this vector
  truncated  BOOL         NOT NULL,         -- article was longer than the model reads
  embedding  VECTOR(1024) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (lang, page_id),
  -- M=16 instead of the default 6: with 1024 dimensions, M=6 found only 79% of the true top 10
  -- (see index_recall.py and the README, step 8).
  VECTOR INDEX (embedding) M=16 DISTANCE=cosine
);

-- The category tree under "Suomen historia" (Finnish category names, without "Luokka:").
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS category_link (
  parent  VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  child   VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (parent, child),
  KEY (child)
) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;

-- Which categories each article is in. Categories come from Finnish Wikipedia; the Swedish and
-- English articles get the categories of the Finnish article on the same topic (same wikidata_id).

  lang      CHAR(2)      NOT NULL,
  page_id   INT UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  category  VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (lang, page_id, category),
  KEY (category)
) CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;

"""How close does the vector index get to the exact answer, and how fast?

    python index_recall.py                        # ef_search 20 ... 640 on the current index
    python index_recall.py --ef 20,100 --runs 5

The vector index (HNSW) is approximate: it walks a graph instead of comparing the question with
every vector. For each test question this script gets the exact top 10 (index switched off, all
vectors compared) and the index's top 10, and reports recall@10 = how many of the exact 10 the
index found. Two settings decide it:
  M          links per node in the graph, fixed when the index is built:  VECTOR INDEX (...) M=16
  ef_search  how many candidates a search looks at, per session:          SET mhnsw_ef_search = 100
"""
import argparse, csv, statistics, time
from common import connect, embed, vector_text

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--ef", default="20,40,80,160,320,640", help="mhnsw_ef_search values to try")
parser.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=3, help="repeat each query this many times for timing")
args = parser.parse_args()

# The vector search on its own, with ORDER BY distance LIMIT directly on article_vector:
# the shape the optimizer needs to use the vector index.
INDEXED = """SELECT lang, page_id FROM article_vector
             ORDER BY VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(embedding, VEC_FromText(?)) LIMIT 10"""
EXACT = """SELECT lang, page_id FROM article_vector IGNORE INDEX (embedding)
           ORDER BY VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(embedding, VEC_FromText(?)) LIMIT 10"""

con = connect()
cur = con.cursor()
cur.execute("SELECT @@version, @@mhnsw_max_cache_size")
version, cache = cur.fetchone()
cur.execute("SHOW CREATE TABLE article_vector")
index_line = [l.strip() for l in cur.fetchone()[1].splitlines() if "VECTOR KEY" in l][0]
print(f"MariaDB {version}, {index_line}, mhnsw_max_cache_size = {cache / 2**20:.0f} MB\n")

with open("data/test-questions.tsv") as f:
    vectors = [vector_text(embed([q["question"]])[0][0]) for q in csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t")]


def timed(sql, v):
    times = []
    for _ in range(args.runs):
        t = time.perf_counter()
        cur.execute(sql, (v,))
        rows = cur.fetchall()
        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1000)
    return set(rows), times


exact, exact_ms = [], []
for v in vectors:
    rows, ms = timed(EXACT, v)
    exact.append(rows)
    exact_ms += ms
print("| ef_search | recall@10 | worst question | median ms | slowest ms |")
print("|---|---|---|---|---|")
print(f"| exact (no index) | 100% | 100% | {statistics.median(exact_ms):.1f} | {max(exact_ms):.1f} |")
for ef in [int(x) for x in args.ef.split(",")]:
    cur.execute(f"SET mhnsw_ef_search = {ef}")
    recalls, all_ms = [], []
    for v, truth in zip(vectors, exact):
        rows, ms = timed(INDEXED, v)
        recalls.append(len(rows & truth) / len(truth))
        all_ms += ms
    print(f"| {ef} | {statistics.mean(recalls):.0%} | {min(recalls):.0%} "
          f"| {statistics.median(all_ms):.1f} | {max(all_ms):.1f} |")
con.close()

"""Cut our articles out of FineWiki and save them as data/articles-<lang>.parquet.

You do not need to run this: the result is published (see README, step 3).
It is here so you can see how it was made, or make your own topic.

    python prepare.py fi          # the Finnish articles in data/articles-fi.tsv  (~5 min)
    python prepare.py sv en       # the Swedish and English articles on the same topics

Finnish articles are matched by page_id; Swedish and English ones by wikidata_id
(the same topic has the same Wikidata id in every language), so run fi first.

DuckDB reads the Parquet files straight from Hugging Face and fetches only the columns we
ask for: the raw wikitext column, about two thirds of every file, is never downloaded.
Each source file is saved separately in data/cache/, so an interrupted run continues
where it stopped.
"""
import sys, time, pathlib, duckdb, requests

REPO = "HuggingFaceFW/finewiki"
COLUMNS = """page_id, version AS rev_id, wikidata_id, title, url, date_modified, text"""
WAIT = 300      # seconds to wait when Hugging Face says "too many requests"

cache = pathlib.Path("data/cache")
cache.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
db = duckdb.connect()
db.sql("SET enable_progress_bar = false")


def source_files(lang):
    """The Parquet files of one language in FineWiki, e.g. data/fiwiki/000_00000.parquet."""
    r = requests.get(f"https://huggingface.co/api/datasets/{REPO}/tree/main/data/{lang}wiki")
    r.raise_for_status()
    return sorted(f["path"] for f in r.json() if f["path"].endswith(".parquet"))


def wanted(lang):
    """A SQL condition that picks our articles in this language."""
    if lang == "fi":
        return "page_id IN (SELECT page_id FROM read_csv('data/articles-fi.tsv', delim='\t'))"
    if not pathlib.Path("data/articles-fi.parquet").exists():
        sys.exit("Run 'python prepare.py fi' first: other languages are matched to the Finnish articles.")
    return ("wikidata_id IN (SELECT wikidata_id FROM 'data/articles-fi.parquet' "
            "WHERE wikidata_id IS NOT NULL)")


for lang in sys.argv[1:] or ["fi"]:
    files = source_files(lang)
    parts = []
    for i, path in enumerate(files, 1):
        part = cache / f"{lang}-{pathlib.Path(path).stem}.parquet"
        parts.append(str(part))
        if part.exists():
            print(f"{lang} {i}/{len(files)} {path}: already done")
            continue
        t = time.time()
        url = f"https://huggingface.co/datasets/{REPO}/resolve/main/{path}"
        tmp = part.with_suffix(".tmp")
        while True:
            try:
                db.sql(f"""COPY (SELECT '{lang}' AS lang, {COLUMNS} FROM read_parquet('{url}')
                                 WHERE {wanted(lang)})
                           TO '{tmp}' (FORMAT parquet)""")
                break
            except duckdb.HTTPException as e:
                # Reading single columns takes ~3,000 small requests per file, and Hugging Face
                # limits how many an anonymous user may make in 5 minutes. Wait and try again.
                if "429" not in str(e):
                    raise
                print(f"  Hugging Face says 'too many requests'. Waiting {WAIT // 60} minutes ...")
                time.sleep(WAIT)
        tmp.rename(part)
        n = db.sql(f"SELECT count(*) FROM '{part}'").fetchone()[0]
        print(f"{lang} {i}/{len(files)} {path}: {n} articles, {time.time() - t:.0f} s")

    # FineWiki sometimes has several versions of one article (e.g. 4 of "Talvisota"): keep the newest.
    out = f"data/articles-{lang}.parquet"
    db.sql(f"""COPY (SELECT * FROM read_parquet({parts})
                     QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY page_id ORDER BY rev_id DESC) = 1
                     ORDER BY page_id)
               TO '{out}' (FORMAT parquet)""")
    n, mb = db.sql(f"SELECT count(*), sum(length(text)) / 1e6 FROM '{out}'").fetchone()
    print(f"Done: {n} {lang} articles, {mb:.0f} MB of text -> {out}")

"""Find every Finnish article in the category "Suomen historia" and its subcategories.

Then adds the main article of every named category one level deeper: famous people and things
have a category of their own, with their article inside it (Luokka:Urho Kekkonen holds the article
Urho Kekkonen). Walking that whole level would double the set with lists of politicians and
councillors; taking only these main articles adds ~460, including the presidents.

Writes three files, takes about 10 minutes:
  data/articles-fi.tsv            page_id, title, level (how deep below the root it was found)
  data/category-links-fi.tsv      parent category, subcategory — the category tree
  data/article-categories-fi.tsv  page_id, category — which categories each article is in
You only need this to rebuild them; the files are in the repo.

Run:  python find_articles.py
"""
import sys, time, requests

API = "https://fi.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"
ROOT = "Luokka:Suomen historia"
LEVELS = 3      # how many levels of subcategories to follow (3 gives about 19,000 articles)
PAUSE = 0.4     # seconds between requests, to stay under Wikipedia's 200 requests/minute

session = requests.Session()
session.headers["User-Agent"] = "mariadb-vector-wikipedia-rag/1.0 (https://github.com/MariaDB/mariadb-vector-wikipedia-rag)"


def api_all(params, key):
    """Call the Wikipedia API and follow 'continue' until the whole list is read."""
    params = dict(params, format="json", formatversion="2")
    while True:
        time.sleep(PAUSE)
        r = session.get(API, params=params, timeout=60)
        if r.status_code != 200:
            wait = int(r.headers.get("Retry-After", 10))
            print(f"  Wikipedia answered {r.status_code}, waiting {wait} s ...", file=sys.stderr)
            time.sleep(wait)
            continue
        data = r.json()
        yield from data["query"][key]
        if "continue" not in data:
            return
        params.update(data["continue"])


def name(title):
    return title.removeprefix("Luokka:")


categories = {ROOT}
articles = {}                   # page_id -> (title, level)
links = set()                   # (parent category, subcategory)
memberships = set()             # (page_id, category)
deeper = {}                     # category one level below the walk -> its parent
this_level = [ROOT]
for level in range(LEVELS + 1):
    next_level = []
    for cat in this_level:
        for m in api_all({"action": "query", "list": "categorymembers", "cmtitle": cat,
                          "cmlimit": "500", "cmprop": "ids|title"}, "categorymembers"):
            if m["ns"] == 14 and level < LEVELS:                                   # a category
                links.add((name(cat), name(m["title"])))
                if m["title"] not in categories:
                    categories.add(m["title"])
                    next_level.append(m["title"])
            elif m["ns"] == 14:                                    # a category one level deeper
                deeper.setdefault(m["title"], cat)
            elif m["ns"] == 0:                                                     # an article
                articles.setdefault(m["pageid"], (m["title"], level))
                memberships.add((m["pageid"], name(cat)))
    print(f"level {level}: {len(categories)} categories, {len(articles)} articles", file=sys.stderr)
    this_level = next_level

# Named categories one level deeper: is there an article with exactly the category's name?
candidates = [c for c in deeper if c not in categories]
named = 0
for i in range(0, len(candidates), 50):
    batch = candidates[i:i + 50]
    for page in api_all({"action": "query", "titles": "|".join(name(c) for c in batch)}, "pages"):
        category = "Luokka:" + page.get("title", "")
        if page.get("missing") or page["ns"] != 0 or page["pageid"] in articles or category not in deeper:
            continue
        articles[page["pageid"]] = (page["title"], LEVELS + 1)
        links.add((name(deeper[category]), page["title"]))
        memberships.add((page["pageid"], page["title"]))
        named += 1
print(f"named categories one level deeper: {named} main articles added", file=sys.stderr)

with open("data/articles-fi.tsv", "w") as f:
    f.write("page_id\ttitle\tlevel\n")
    for page_id, (title, level) in sorted(articles.items()):
        f.write(f"{page_id}\t{title}\t{level}\n")
with open("data/category-links-fi.tsv", "w") as f:
    f.write("parent\tchild\n")
    for parent, child in sorted(links):
        f.write(f"{parent}\t{child}\n")
with open("data/article-categories-fi.tsv", "w") as f:
    f.write("page_id\tcategory\n")
    for page_id, cat in sorted(memberships):
        f.write(f"{page_id}\t{cat}\n")
print(f"Done: {len(articles)} articles, {len(categories)} categories, {len(links)} category links, "
      f"{len(memberships)} article-category pairs -> data/")

            os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value.strip())

# --- Database. The defaults match docker-compose.yml (port 3307, so it does not collide with

DB = dict(host=os.environ.get("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
          port=int(os.environ.get("DB_PORT", 3307)),
          user=os.environ.get("DB_USER", "wikirag"),
          password=[REDACTED]"DB_PASSWORD", "wikirag"),
          database=os.environ.get("DB_NAME", "wikirag"))

# --- Embedding model, run by Ollama on this machine. ---
OLLAMA = os.environ.get("OLLAMA_URL", "http://localhost:11434")
MODEL = "bge-m3"
CONTEXT = 8192   # tokens bge-m3 can read.
# Ollama needs both settings: num_ctx alone is not enough. An embedding must fit in one
# batch, and Ollama's default batch is 2,048 tokens, so longer texts are refused or cut.
OPTIONS = {"num_ctx": CONTEXT, "num_batch": CONTEXT}


# How many candidates a vector index search looks at (default 20). With M=16, 80 found 100% of
# the exact top 10 for our test questions in ~5 ms (index_recall.py).
EF_SEARCH = 80


def connect():
    con = mariadb.connect(**DB, autocommit=False)
    con.cursor().execute(f"SET mhnsw_ef_search = {EF_SEARCH}")
    return con


def embed(texts, truncate=True):
    """Turn a list of texts into vectors with the embedding model.

    With truncate=False, Ollama refuses texts longer than CONTEXT instead of cutting them,
    which is how embed.py finds out which articles are too long.
    Returns (vectors, number of tokens read).
    """
    r = requests.post(f"{OLLAMA}/api/embed", timeout=600, json={
        "model": MODEL, "input": texts, "truncate": truncate,
        "options": OPTIONS})
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise ValueError(r.text)
    data = r.json()
    return data["embeddings"], data.get("prompt_eval_count", 0)


def vector_text(vector):
    """MariaDB reads a vector from text like '[0.1,0.2,...]' with VEC_FromText()."""
    return json.dumps(vector)


# --- The searches. search.py, app.py and evaluate.py all use these. ---

# Vector search, no category. The vector search stands alone in a subquery: ORDER BY the
# distance, LIMIT, on article_vector only. That is the shape in which MariaDB uses the vector
# index (~5 ms). Written as one flat JOIN, the same query read ~22,000 rows and took ~50 ms.
VECTOR_SQL = """
SELECT a.lang, a.page_id, a.wikidata_id, a.title, a.url, v.distance
FROM (SELECT lang, page_id, VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(embedding, VEC_FromText(?)) AS distance
      FROM article_vector
      {where}
      ORDER BY distance
      LIMIT ?) AS v
JOIN article a USING (lang, page_id)
ORDER BY v.distance"""

# A category and all its subcategories, found by walking the category tree (recursive CTE).
# CAST: the first row sets the column size, and subcategory names can be longer.
CATEGORY_TREE = """
WITH RECURSIVE cats AS (
  SELECT CAST(? AS VARCHAR(255)) AS name
  UNION
  SELECT l.child FROM category_link l JOIN cats ON l.parent = cats.name)"""

IN_CATEGORY = """EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM article_category c JOIN cats ON c.category = cats.name
              WHERE c.lang = a.lang AND c.page_id = a.page_id)"""

# Vector search inside a category: one statement. MariaDB picks the category's articles first
# and compares only those, exactly - fast for small categories, slower for big ones (README).
VECTOR_IN_CATEGORY_SQL = CATEGORY_TREE + """
SELECT a.lang, a.page_id, a.wikidata_id, a.title, a.url,
       VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(v.embedding, VEC_FromText(?)) AS distance
FROM article_vector v
JOIN article a USING (lang, page_id)
WHERE """ + IN_CATEGORY + """
  {and_lang}
ORDER BY distance
LIMIT ?"""

KEYWORD_SQL = """{tree}
SELECT a.lang, a.page_id, a.wikidata_id, a.title, a.url,
       MATCH(a.title, a.text) AGAINST (?) AS score
FROM article a
WHERE MATCH(a.title, a.text) AGAINST (?) {and_lang} {and_category}
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT ?"""


def search(cur, question, mode="vector", lang=None, category=None, limit=10, vector=None):
    """Run one search. Returns (sql, rows); each row is a dict.

    mode "vector": semantic search - the question is embedded with the same model as the
    articles, and MariaDB returns the closest vectors (smaller distance = closer).
    Pass vector= to skip embedding the question (evaluate.py does, to time the two apart).
    mode "keyword": MariaDB's ordinary full-text search (higher score = better match).
    lang: only fi, sv or en. category: only this Finnish category and its subcategories.
    """
    if mode == "keyword":
        sql = KEYWORD_SQL.format(tree=CATEGORY_TREE if category else "",
                                 and_lang="AND a.lang = ?" if lang else "",
                                 and_category="AND " + IN_CATEGORY if category else "")
        params = ([category] if category else []) + [question, question] + ([lang] if lang else []) + [limit]
    else:
        if vector is None:
            [vector], _ = embed([question])
        if category:
            sql = VECTOR_IN_CATEGORY_SQL.format(and_lang="AND a.lang = ?" if lang else "")
            params = [category, vector_text(vector)] + ([lang] if lang else []) + [limit]
        else:
            sql = VECTOR_SQL.format(where="WHERE lang = ?" if lang else "")
            params = [vector_text(vector)] + ([lang] if lang else []) + [limit]
    cur.execute(sql, params)
    columns = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
    return sql.strip(), [dict(zip(columns, row)) for row in cur.fetchall()]


def other_languages(cur, rows):
    """For each result, the same topic in the other languages: {wikidata_id: [(lang, title, url)]}."""
    ids = {r["wikidata_id"] for r in rows if r["wikidata_id"]}
    if not ids:
        return {}
    cur.execute(f"SELECT wikidata_id, lang, title, url FROM article WHERE wikidata_id IN "
                f"({', '.join('?' * len(ids))}) ORDER BY lang", list(ids))
    found = {}
    for wikidata_id, lang, title, url in cur.fetchall():
        found.setdefault(wikidata_id, []).append((lang, title, url))
    return found

              (lang, page_id, rev_id, wikidata_id, title, url, date_modified, text)
              VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""", rows)
    print(f"{path}: {len(rows)} articles")
print("Articles in the table:", count("article"))

# ... which the Swedish and English articles on the same topic inherit.

               SELECT other.lang, other.page_id, c.category
               FROM article_category c
               JOIN article fi    ON fi.lang = 'fi' AND fi.page_id = c.page_id
               JOIN article other ON other.wikidata_id = fi.wikidata_id AND other.lang <> 'fi'
               WHERE c.lang = 'fi'""")

    for lang in ("en", "fi", "sv"):
        path = f"data/vectors-{MODEL}-{lang}.parquet"
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            print(f"Downloading {path} ...")
            with requests.get(f"{RELEASE}/{os.path.basename(path)}", stream=True, timeout=60) as r:
                r.raise_for_status()
                with open(path + ".part", "wb") as f:
                    for chunk in r.iter_content(1 << 20):
                        f.write(chunk)
            os.rename(path + ".part", path)
        t = time.time()
        table = pq.read_table(path)
        # MariaDB takes a VECTOR as raw bytes: 1024 float32 numbers, little-endian.
        rows = [(r["lang"], r["page_id"], r["model"], r["truncated"],
                 struct.pack(f"<{len(r['embedding'])}f", *r["embedding"]))
                for r in table.to_pylist()]
        insert("""INSERT IGNORE INTO article_vector (lang, page_id, model, truncated, embedding)
                  VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""", rows)
        print(f"{path}: {len(rows)} vectors, {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
    print("Vectors in the table:", count("article_vector"))
